I've implemented the support ticket MCP server in `server.mjs`. Here's a summary of the changes:

## What was broken
`server.mjs` was a stub: `listTools()` returned an empty array and `callTool()` returned `{content:[]}` with no text, so the `creates` test failed trying to read `r.content[0].text`.

## What I implemented

**`listTools()`** — advertises a single `ticket_create` tool with an `inputSchema` that:
- requires `title` and `description` (strings)
- defines `priority` as an enum `[low, normal, high]` with `default: 'normal'`
- sets `additionalProperties: false` (no extra fields)

**`callTool(name, args)`** — the core logic:
- **Unknown tool rejection**: any name other than `ticket_create` throws `Unknown tool: ...` (the protocol's catch turns this into a JSON-RPC error).
- **Argument validation**:
  - rejects non-object args
  - rejects any key outside the allowed `title`/`description`/`priority` set (no extra fields)
  - requires `title` and `description` to be non-empty strings (whitespace-only rejected too)
  - validates `priority` against the enum; defaults to `normal` when omitted
- **Stable sequential ids**: a module-level counter produces `t1`, `t2`, `t3`, … in creation order.
- **Concise text result**: returns `{ content: [{ type: 'text', text }] }` like `Created ticket t1 "Bug" (priority: normal)`.

## Verification
- The provided `creates` test passes (matches `t1` and `normal`).
- I also sanity-checked sequential ids, default/bad priority, missing/empty title & description, extra fields, and unknown-tool rejection — all behave correctly.
- The full suite (`node --test`) is green: 1 pass, 0 fail.
